content: Gynazole-1, also known as butoconazole nitrate cream, is a medication used to treat vaginal yeast infections. It works by reducing symptoms such as vaginal burning, itching, and discharge associated with this condition. This medication belongs to the azole antifungal class. The standard dosage involves applying one applicator full of cream (approximately 5 grams) intravaginally as a single dose. In pregnant women during the second and third trimesters, treatment may need to be extended for up to six days. However, the safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established for use during the first trimester of pregnancy. Before using this medication, inform your doctor if you are allergic to butoconazole or other azole antifungal agents (e.g., clotrimazole, fluconazole) or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Additionally, it contains mineral oil, which can weaken latex or rubber products such as condoms, diaphragms, or cervical caps, potentially leading to failure. Avoid using these products during treatment and for three days after completing treatment. To use the medication, wash your hands before and after application. Lie on your back with your knees bent toward your chest, and insert the applicator filled with the cream into the vagina as far as it comfortably goes. Avoid using tampons or douches while undergoing treatment. If the cream comes into contact with your eyes, rinse them immediately with plenty of water. Follow all preparation and usage instructions provided in the product package. If your condition does not improve or recurs within two months, consult your doctor. Common side effects may include increased vaginal or urethral burning, itching, pain, or mild abdominal cramps. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. If you experience severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, seek emergency medical attention immediately. For non-emergency overdoses, contact a poison control center. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, and pregnant women should exercise extra caution when using the vaginal applicator. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. To prevent vaginal yeast infections, thoroughly dry the genital area after bathing, showering, or swimming. Avoid wearing tight jeans, nylon underwear, pantyhose, wet bathing suits, or damp exercise clothes for extended periods. Store this medication at room temperature. Do not flush it down the toilet or pour it into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
